To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the ability of blood lymphocytes from cancer patients to respond to sheep erythrocytes in vitro, as determined by the number of haemolysin-formin g cell foci, was lower than in normal controls, 2) the depression of antibody production in cancer patients was more pronounced in patients with regional lymph node metastasis than in those with no regional metastasis, 3) the difference between patients with regional metastasis and patients without regional metastasis remained significant after

(1) the ability of lymphocytes to produce a primary anti-SRBC antibody response in vitro is depressed in cancer patients, and (2) this depression is more marked when lymph node involvement is detected.

a) peripheral blood lymphocytes from cancer patients are capable of producing antibodies in vitro, and that the response is specific; b) cancer patients produce fewer antibody-forming cells than controls, and that the depression is related to the clinical stage of the disease; c) in the absence of any other explanation, the results suggest that the depression of the immune response is due to the tumor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the in vitro production of antibody in peripheral blood lymphocytes from cancer patients.
an immunological test which can be used to detect the presence of metastatic cancer in the lymph nodes of breast cancer patients.
the possibility of using a lymphocyte culture system to detect a biological marker of early cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

antibody production in vitro by peripheral blood lymphocytes from early breast cancer patients may be a useful tool for predicting the presence of metastatic growth within the regional lymph nodes, but not for predicting distant metastatic spread.

the in vitro antibody response to sheep erythrocytes of peripheral blood lymphocytes from early breast cancer patients is not depressed in the absence of regional lymph node metastases but is definitely depressed in the presence of such metastases.

the primary antibody response of peripheral blood lymphocytes to sheep red blood cells, as assessed in vitro in soft agar, was depressed in patients with early breast carcinoma and that the extent of this depression was correlated with the extent of regional lymph node involvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antibody response of lymphocytes from breast-cancer-bearing women, as assessed by the hemolytic plaque assay, is depressed in N1 patients and not in N0 patients.

the primary antibody response of peripheral blood lymphocytes from early breast cancer patients is significantly depressed, and that the depression is related to the presence of regional lymph node metastases.

, in the absence of distant metastasis, the antibody production of breast cancer patients is not impaired, but that the number of antibody-forming cells decreases as the regional lymph nodes become invaded by cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the primary antibody response in cultured blood lymph cells from breast cancer patients can be depressed by the disease, and that this depression is related to the presence of lymph node metastasis.
the in vitro antibody response of peripheral lymphocytes from cancer patients is depressed in comparison with healthy controls.
the antibody production in vitro of blood lymphocytes of patients with early breast cancers is depressed when regional lymph nodes are invaded by the tumour.
